watchouts.what_to_do: Give it 8-12 weeks; pairs well with vitamin C or niacinamide to layer complementary brightening.

benefits.mechanism: Arbutin is a competitive, reversible inhibitor of tyrosinase, reducing melanin synthesis at non-cytotoxic concentrations in human melanocyte culture (mechanism study, PMID 8632348).
benefits.what_it_means: Gradually brightens and fades the look of dark spots and uneven tone over 8-12 weeks.

evidence.summary: Competitive reversible tyrosinase inhibition demonstrated in human melanocyte culture and skin-tissue models; graded B.

citations.title: Arbutin: mechanism of its depigmenting action in human melanocyte culture
citations.source: Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics; PMID 8632348

citations.title: Inhibitory effects of arbutin on melanin biosynthesis of alpha-MSH-induced hyperpigmentation in cultured skin tissues

overview: Arbutin gently brightens and evens tone by slowing melanin production, delivering a milder, gradual alternative to harsher brightening agents.

ingredient.what_it_is: A naturally derived glucoside of hydroquinone that releases its brightening action slowly and gently, making it a milder, non-photoreactive tone-evening ingredient.

marketing_vs_reality.reality: It is a glucoside that releases its active slowly, which makes it far gentler and, unlike some depigmenting agents, non-photoreactive — but also more gradual in effect.
